extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, PTAB attorneys, IP litigators
extracted.subtask_description: Summaries of recent PTAB/Director decisions highlighting legal standards and procedural rulings in post-issuance proceedings (IPR/PGR), useful for practitioners handling PTAB matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of multiple dependent claim limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Director Vidal explains that the Board must consider each separately incorporated claim limitation in determining patentability of multiple dependent claims and, here, patentability of one of the independent claims incorporated by reference in multiple dependent claims renders those multiple dependent claims patentable as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precedential decision on rehearing (Nested Bean, Inc. v. Big Beings Pty Ltd., IPR2020-01234, Paper 42). When evaluating multiple dependent claims, the Board must assess the patentability impact of each incorporated limitation individually; patentability of an incorporated independent claim can render the multiple dependent claims patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fintiv factor analysis before compelling-merits test
rubrics_metrics.description: On sua sponte review, Director Vidal vacated an institution decision where Board failed to consider Fintiv factors 1-5 before finding compelling merits to institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CommScope Techs. LLC. v. Dali Wireless, Inc., IPR2022-01242, Paper 23: The panel must first consider whether Fintiv factors 1-5 favor discretionary denial; only if those factors do not justify denial should the Board then perform the compelling merits analysis. Boards should explicitly evaluate Fintiv factors before invoking the compelling-merits exception to discretionary denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for public filing of designated confidential information
rubrics_metrics.description: Director ordered a party to show cause why it should not be sanctioned for publicly filing information previously designated confidential to the parties and Board, and denied a request to make the information public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Quality Assurance, LLC v. VLSI Technology LLC, IPR2021-01229, Paper 117: Practitioners should avoid publicly filing materials designated confidential; doing so can trigger show-cause orders and potential sanctions. Requests to unseal must be addressed through proper procedure; unilateral public filing is risky.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB jurisdiction when claim already invalidated in district court
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board denied IPR institution because it lacked jurisdiction to cancel a claim invalidated under section 101 in an earlier district court decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Volvo Penta of the Americas, LLC v. Brunswick Corporation, IPR2022-01424, Paper 12: If a claim has already been invalidated in district court (e.g., under §101), the PTAB may lack jurisdiction to institute review to cancel that claim. Check preexisting district court rulings for impacts on PTAB jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differing testimony cannot establish definiteness
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board denied a Motion to Amend where Patent Owner’s own witnesses gave differing meanings to a term in the substitute claims (different but overlapping values for 'high pressure').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Halliburton Energy Services, Inc. v. US Well Services, LLC, IPR2021-01316, Paper 44: Inconsistent or differing expert/witness testimony about claim term meanings undermines a showing of definiteness; harmonized, consistent testimony is necessary to support definiteness of amended claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: No need for adverse-judgment motion after statutory disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner’s request for leave to file a motion for adverse judgment was denied where the Patent Owner previously filed a statutory disclaimer resulting in an adverse judgment against it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early Warning Services, LLC v. Fintech Innovation Associates, LLC, PGR2022-00046, Paper 18: If a patent owner has already effectively produced an adverse outcome (e.g., via statutory disclaimer), petitioners may not be permitted to seek a separate adverse-judgment motion; consider prior patent-owner actions before pursuing such motions.
